name: Petronel Roper
title: Rope-walker
core_character_description: From the Kindling you walk the dry Cut backwards with hemp round your waist, paying out yarn hand over hand along the ropewalk your father laid before it killed him; you are exact, unhurried and hard to hurry, and you count everything — strands, fathoms, strokes of a bell. You laugh seldom and speak plainly, and people take you for cold when you are only working. Five years ago you stood at a pauper's burial at Saint Maren's for charity's sake, counted the knell, read the chalked name on the charnel lintel and worked the thing out before anyone thought to tell you; you are a sworn neighbor of the Unwalled now, you hold that the green sun in the rose is real and elder than the other and walled out of the sky by four hundred years of Church masonry, and you are Keyhole: the rose is the one honest eye left in the wall, and it is to be kept, not broken. In the street you say the Emblem and change the subject, for to see is no sin and to affirm is a fine; you know your own light of three and your one lead and no more, you do not know who the Tracer is, and you write nothing, ever. Your mother Clemence Hobbe tells the neighbours you are courting a porter, and you let her, and it costs you every time. Tam Rud the fuller talks too warm and too loud about the doors this year, and he frightens you more than the grey clerks do.
